display.purpose: The name on the home terminus only; Archivo at weight 800, width 118%.

title.purpose: Station headings and door labels; ring position derives from its size.

item.purpose: List titles for projects, posts and destinations.

prose.purpose: Long reading, 65ch max; opened up at night.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: The line-diagram surfaces are flat. Night depth comes from shader bloom on pulsing routes (0.35 strength at 7px sigma), not box-shadow. The build carries no box-shadow or drop-shadow anywhere; interior edges are borders. daisyUI themes set --depth 0 and --noise 0, so buttons, alerts and menus are flat as well.

motion.name: trunk-lit
motion.value: clip-path inset from (0 0 calc(100% - 50vh) 0) to 0, linear, animation-timeline: scroll(root)
motion.purpose: The lit trunk starts lit to mid-screen and the edge travels with the reader. Needs animation-timeline support and no-preference motion; otherwise the whole line is lit.

motion.name: train-ride
motion.purpose: The vehicle rides the lit edge on the same scroll range as the trunk. display:none unless supported and motion allowed.

motion.name: signature-wipe
motion.value: clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) to inset(0), linear, view() range entry 0% to entry 100%
motion.purpose: Signature written left to right on entry; shown whole when motion is off.

motion.name: ring-light
motion.purpose: A door lights its ring with the branch color on hover or focus-within; transition none under reduced motion.

motion.name: arrow-nudge
motion.value: transform translate 4px on group hover (down on doors, right on lists)
motion.purpose: Affordance on rows; motion-reduce disables the transition.

motion.name: theme-dissolve
motion.purpose: Theme switch crossfades; skipped under reduced motion or without startViewTransition. The sun/moon and burger/X swap-rotate icons are daisyUI swaps.

motion.name: page-fade
motion.value: svelte fade 200ms cubicOut; 0 whenever view transitions are in use or motion is reduced
motion.purpose: Route change fallback where startViewTransition is missing.

motion.name: network-draw-in
motion.value: 2.4s, easeOutCubic (1-(1-x)^3); station rings appear staggered 0.05 per index
motion.purpose: The WebGL map draws itself in on load; reduced motion starts at 1 (finished).

motion.name: network-pulses
motion.value: two comet pulses per route, speeds 100 to 210 px/s, tail 70px, head 6px; bright core mixes toward white 75% at night, base*0.55 by day
motion.purpose: Light travels the routes; uPulse is 0 under reduced motion.

motion.name: network-lens
motion.value: gaussian radius 150px, pull 0.38; stations grow up to 35% within 130px; parallax up to 7px x, 5px y; smoothing 0.18 / 0.08 / 0.06
motion.purpose: Cursor bends nearby lines and enlarges stations. Disabled for coarse pointers and reduced motion.

motion.name: page-view-transition
motion.value: onNavigate wraps client navigation in document.startViewTransition when supported and prefers-reduced-motion is not reduce; ::view-transition-group(*) 0.5s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)
motion.purpose: Pages cross-fade and shared elements morph. Navbar theme switch uses its own transition (0.4s root).

motion.name: shared-image-morph
motion.value: view-transition-name: p-{slug} on the project image in the list and on the project page
motion.purpose: A project picture travels from its list tile to the project page. Tiles with no image have no name.

motion.name: project-tile-hover
motion.value: filter transition 200ms, brightness 1.1 on group hover; none under reduced motion
motion.purpose: Affordance on project tiles, with title underline.

motion.name: route-strip-current
motion.value: scroll listener (rAF-throttled, passive): the current stop is the last h2 whose top is above 45% of the viewport height, the first until then; sets aria-current=location on the matching menu link
motion.purpose: Marks the stop nearest the reading position as the active (brand purple) menu item. The small-screen collapse-arrow is drawn by daisyUI; no hand-made chevron.

motion.name: copy-toast
motion.value: svelte fade 150ms on a daisyUI toast (toast-end toast-bottom, alert-success); Copied state lasts 1800ms
motion.purpose: Confirms a copy visibly; aria-hidden, the separate status region announces it.

motion.name: signal-tower
motion.value: three.js orthographic scene: yaw 0.55 + sin(t*0.4)*0.07 + (overall-0.5)*0.5 + lean; train eases toward the reading line (exp 9/s); active ring scale 1.45, hot ring 1.2 (both 1.74); pulses fall at 0.9 units/s and vanish 0.15 above the train
motion.purpose: The home-page rail mirrors scroll position as a lit spine and train. Reduced motion: no ambient sine, no pulses, eased values snap, redrawn on demand.

motion.name: train-ride-end
motion.purpose: The marker ends its ride just short of the page end.

breakpoints.name: xl (route strip aside, 3-up projects, CMS 70ch + 15rem grid)
xl (signal tower rail on the home page; three.js loaded via min-width 80rem)

webgl.api: WebGL2, one fragment shader, fullscreen triangle, no library; premultiplied alpha, antialias off, powerPreference low-power
webgl.routes: 6 (3 door lines purple/teal/amber at 3.5px half-width, alpha 0.95; 3 quiet routes at 2.25px, alpha 0.5/0.42/0.42), max 64 segments and 40 stations
webgl.geometry: octilinear, grid g = clamp(w/44, 24, 34)px (14px under 700px); door routes start at the data-route-start arrows
webgl.stations: rings at each door start (10.5px radius, 7px narrow) and alternate bends (8px), plus interchanges (9px) where different routes cross; ring holes are filled with the page ground colour (gray-50 / gray-950), not white; max 40
webgl.calm: up to 4 data-calm boxes fade the map to 0.1 within 110px; map also dissolves into the page over the last 140px
webgl.pixelBudget: dpr capped at 1.5 (1.25 coarse), area budget 1.4e6 px (0.9e6 coarse); frame time EMA over 26ms after 45 samples drops quality x0.8 down to 0.55
webgl.pause: IntersectionObserver stops it off screen; visibilitychange stops it when the tab is hidden; context loss hides the canvas
webgl.reducedMotion: single finished still frame, redrawn on resize and theme change; no pulses, lens or parallax
webgl.theme: reads --line-*, brand-300/400 and gray ramp from computed styles; MutationObserver on html class re-themes live
webgl.fallback: returns null without WebGL2 and the page simply has no map

focus.ring: :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid brand-500; outline-offset: 2px } and brand-300 under .dark
focus.skipLink: sr-only until focus, then fixed top-left, brand-600 fill, white text

extensions.baseText: body colour is set in the base layer: gray-900 by day, white at night (tinted ink, not the browser default)
extensions.darkMode: html.dark class and html[data-theme] ('line-night' dark, 'line' light) set together by a pre-paint inline script in app.html (from localStorage 'darkmode', falling back to prefers-color-scheme; light leaves data-theme unset so the default theme 'line' applies) and by the darkmode store in stores.js on every change; Tailwind custom variant dark = .dark

interiorPages.terminus: .terminus-page: --pt 6.5rem (8rem from 48rem); --ring-top = --pt + --page-size/2; --page-size clamp(2rem, 1.5rem + 2vw, 3rem). Links page sets its own --pt/--av so the ring centres on the avatar (5rem, 7rem from sm).
interiorPages.endStation: Station component with end: closing station covers the trunk below its ring. CMS 'Next stop' (next page or Projects) and project 'Keep riding' are line contact; projects list uses cycled colour on its last year.
interiorPages.colourCycle: Stations cycle line-work, line-writing, line-contact by position (3n: work, 3n+2: writing, 3n: contact) for project years, link rows and CMS h2s.
interiorPages.projects: Grouped by year, each year a station; grid 1 / 2 (sm) / 3 (xl) columns; tile = 16:9 image (width=1000 webp, lazy) + Item title, no chrome; gray placeholder block when no image; project page shows 'Stop N of M' with a progress bar, then the year, and image + 65ch prose.
interiorPages.links: Avatar (CMS serves the profile picture only at width 200, 600 or 1200; the page requests 200) is the terminus; rows are stations with --ring-top 50% and min-height 4rem; hover or focus-within fills the ring; socials are btn btn-soft btn-lg rounded-full pills (48px) in the Elsewhere end station.
interiorPages.sshkey: Ticket: 2px bordered rounded-2xl plate, key in bold mono with select-all, dashed divider with two 1.5rem ground-coloured notches, CopyButton; shows an alert alert-warning when the key is unavailable.
interiorPages.error: 404: bar, dashed gap, dashed ring (missing stop), 'This stop isn't on the line.'. Other statuses: two bars with a gap, 'Service interrupted.'. Actions are btn btn-primary 'Back to the start' and btn btn-ghost 'Projects'. Decorative line is aria-hidden.

behaviour.routeStrip: Built client-side from the CMS page's own h2s (ids assigned stop-N when missing). Shown only with more than 3 stops: from xl a sticky aside nav (aria-label 'Stops on this page') holding a menu menu-lg; below xl a daisyUI collapse collapse-arrow (details/summary, base-200) around a menu menu-md. The current stop (scroll-spy: last h2 above 45% of the viewport, first by default) gets aria-current=location in the aside and renders as the active brand-purple menu item. Without scripts there is no strip and the content is intact.
behaviour.foldLists: enhance.js foldLists: any ul/ol with more than 12 items keeps the first 8 and hides the rest (hidden attribute) behind a button.btn.btn-link.btn-sm ('Show N more' / 'Show fewer', aria-expanded toggled). Without scripts every item shows.
behaviour.freshness: localStorage seen:{slug} is compared with date_updated; if the stored value is older, a daisyUI badge badge-primary 'New since your last visit' shows beside the updated date. First visits and unavailable storage show nothing.
behaviour.copyButton: CopyButton: navigator.clipboard.writeText; btn btn-outline btn-sm that gains btn-success and reads 'Copied' for 1800ms; a daisyUI toast (toast-end toast-bottom) with alert-success '{what} copied' fades in (aria-hidden); visually hidden suffix names what is copied; a separate role=status region announces '{what} copied'. If the clipboard fails the text stays selectable.
behaviour.viewTransitions: Layout skips the transition when reduced motion is on or startViewTransition is missing, and turns the 200ms fade off whenever transitions are used or motion is reduced.
behaviour.progressiveEnhancement: Route strip, list fold and freshness badge are enhancements only; CMS content renders whole and readable without scripts. The phone menu is forced open without scripts.
behaviour.navigation: Navbar.svelte: desktop (md up) is a navbar with a menu-horizontal menu-lg list, current page via aria-current=page rendered as the active pill, and a btn-ghost btn-circle swap-rotate sun/moon toggle (aria-label Dark mode, aria-pressed). Phone is a bar on base-200 with a btn-ghost btn-square btn-lg swap-rotate burger/X (aria-label Menu, aria-expanded, aria-controls=mobile-menu) and a btn-lg theme toggle; the menu-lg list closes on Escape, on a pointerdown outside the nav, and when a link is chosen. Phone targets are 48px (btn-lg).
behaviour.alertsAndSkeleton: SSH key missing: alert alert-warning (role=alert). Home blog failure: alert alert-soft (role=status) with a btn btn-sm link. BlogListerLoading: skeleton blocks, animation off under reduced motion.
behaviour.progress: Project page 'Stop N of M' is paired with progress progress-primary (w-28, value N of M, aria-hidden: the text carries the meaning).

cmsContent.keying: All CMS styling is keyed to semantic elements inside .page-content-container, so editors can rewrite pages freely without classes.
cmsContent.rhythm: .page-content-container > * + * margin-top 1rem; li + li 0.35rem; ul padding-left 1.5rem; empty p/h2/h3 hidden; links brand-coloured and underlined.
cmsContent.h2Stations: .ride > h2: ring (1.5rem, 5px border in --line, ground-filled) and 5px stub drawn with ::before / ::after at the h2, positioned left of the content column; --line cycles work / writing (3n+2) / contact (3n); weight 700, tracking -0.01em.
cmsContent.blockquote: Plate: 0.5rem radius, 2px brand-600 border (brand-300 at night), Archivo, white ground (gray-900 at night).
cmsContent.table: Timetable: full width, collapsed borders, tabular numerals; th inverted (brand-600 fill with white text; brand-300 fill with gray-950 text at night), left aligned, 0.55rem 0.75rem padding; td has a gray-300 (gray-700 at night) bottom border.

daisyui.role: UI primitives come from daisyUI 5. The line-diagram pieces (trunk, stations, rings, terminus, ticket, error line, map) are bespoke and not daisyUI.
daisyui.plugin: @plugin 'daisyui' { themes: false; logs: false; include: properties, svg, scrollbar, rootcolor, button, navbar, menu, badge, collapse, swap, toast, alert, skeleton, progress; } in src/app.css. Add a component to the include list only when the site uses it.
daisyui.themes: Two @plugin 'daisyui/theme' blocks: 'line' (default, color-scheme light) and 'line-night' (dark). No stock theme is shipped. @theme static makes the brand and gray variables always exist so the themes can reference them.

themeToTokenMapping.line: base-100/200/300 = gray-50/100/200; base-content gray-900; primary brand-600 (content white); secondary oklch(0.52 0.09 200) teal; accent oklch(0.62 0.14 65) amber (content gray-950); neutral gray-900 (content gray-50); info brand-500; success = teal; warning = amber; error oklch(0.5 0.2 27)
themeToTokenMapping.line-night: base-100/200/300 = gray-950/900/800; base-content white; primary brand-300 (content gray-950); secondary oklch(0.78 0.09 200); accent oklch(0.8 0.14 75); neutral gray-100 (content gray-950); info brand-400; success = night teal; warning = night amber; error oklch(0.7 0.17 25); all contents gray-950
themeToTokenMapping.shared: radius-selector 0.25rem, radius-field 0.5rem, radius-box 0.75rem, size-selector 0.25rem, size-field 0.25rem, border 2px, depth 0, noise 0

daisyui.derivation: Brand and gray values are referenced by var(--color-brand-*) / var(--color-gray-*); the line hues are the same oklch values as --line-writing / --line-contact. A token change flows through to every primitive.
overrides: .menu { --menu-active-bg: var(--color-primary); --menu-active-fg: var(--color-primary-content) } so the active menu item is brand purple, not neutral
Link rule uses :where(li:not(.menu li)) > a (with .link, p > a, .page-content-container a) so daisyUI buttons and menus are not repainted brand-underlined
daisyui.dataThemeMechanism: See darkMode: .dark and data-theme change together in the pre-paint script and in the store.
daisyui.noscript: app.html forces .mobile-menu to display:flex under noscript so phone navigation stays reachable.

signalTower.role: Bespoke line-diagram piece, not daisyUI. Home page only, xl and up. Files: src/lib/Tower.svelte (DOM, links, state), src/lib/tower.js (three.js drawing), src/lib/color.js (oklch token reader).
signalTower.placement: aside.pointer-events-none.absolute.inset-y-0.right-6.z-10.w-60, hidden below xl; inner div pointer-events-auto sticky top-28 mt-40, height min(34rem, 100vh - 9rem).
signalTower.stops: About (only when the welcome text exists, work line), Work (work), Writing (writing), Beyond work (work), Contact (contact). nav aria-label 'Jump to a section', ol of a[href=#id][data-stop] in the t-item role.
signalTower.geometry: Orthographic camera, 64 css px per world unit, tilt 0.5 rad, spine 42px from the rail's left edge. Track cylinder radius 0.05, lit spine 0.075 (runs from the top to the train). Train: capsule radius 0.13 with a ground-coloured back-face outline at 1.28x. Three pulse spheres (0.06). Per station: torus ring (0.22 / 0.055), platform slab 1.7 wide with a line-colour front edge, the 'shelf' placed 0.64 units below its label, a post with a signal lamp, and a glow plane 1.25. Station heights come from the links' measured centres (divided by scale and cos tilt), re-measured on resize and when fonts load.
signalTower.palette: Read from computed styles via color.js: ring, edge, lamp and glow use --line-work / --line-writing / --line-contact per stop; lit spine --line-work; track gray-300 (gray-700 night); slab and post gray-200 (gray-800 night); train --line-work by day, white at night; train outline gray-50 / gray-950 (the ground). Night glow is additive, day glow normal blending at 0.55 strength. A MutationObserver on the html class re-reads the palette on theme change.
signalTower.state: active: the last section whose top is above the reading line (45% of viewport height); ring scale 1.45, glow 0.85, lamp 1.35; the link gets aria-current=location and darker text. hot: pointer enter or focus on a link; ring 1.2, glow 0.55, lamp 1.35. lean: +0.12 rad of yaw while any link is hot, eased. Yaw = 0.55 + slow sine (0.07) + scroll progress (-0.25 to +0.25) + lean.
signalTower.loading: three.js (named imports) is reached only through a dynamic import('./tower.js') in Tower.svelte onMount, only when (min-width: 80rem) matches, as its own chunk (about 533 kB, 132 kB gzip). Never in the main bundle.
signalTower.performance: IntersectionObserver (thresholds 0 and 0.3) pauses drawing below 30% visible; a hidden document pauses; pixel budget 0.9e6 px, dpr capped at 2; low-power context; destroy() disposes geometries, materials, textures and the renderer and forces context loss.
signalTower.reducedMotion: Renders on demand (scroll, resize, theme change, hover change); no ambient sine, no pulses, eased values jump to their targets.
signalTower.accessibility: The shortcut links are the only interactive part; the canvas is aria-hidden and pointer-events-none. Links are real anchors in page order; keyboard focus lights the station like hover; the current stop carries aria-current=location. Label text is gray-700 / gray-300, ink / white when current or hovered. Hover underlines in the stop's line colour (3px, offset 6px).
signalTower.fallback: Without WebGL, or narrower than xl (never loaded), the rail is a plain list: a 6px CSS spine in the hairline colour 42px from the left and a 22px ground-filled ring dot (5px border in the stop's line colour) at each link. The class 'ready', set when the 3D layer is up, hides the CSS spine and dots.

narrative.overview:
The site is one person's hub drawn as a Beck-style transit diagram. One purple trunk runs down the home page; every section is a station hung off it as a ring; the three doors (Work, Writing, Contact) are lines that continue into a living WebGL map behind the hero. By day it is ink on paper; by night it is a glowing map on near-black. Light and dark are equal citizens, switched by the .dark class on html (which also sets the matching daisyUI theme).

The type is signage: Archivo Variable set expanded and heavy for the name, a tight heavy title for each station, Public Sans Variable for everything read. Every neutral shares the brand hue (324.6), so no gray is dead. Color is rationed: purple owns the trunk, links, focus and the name; teal and amber each belong to exactly one branch.

The home page is the full expression of the world, and the interior pages inherit it. Projects, project pages, CMS pages and links are more stops on the same line: the page heading is the terminus, section headings are stations, and the page ends at a closing station that points onward. They use the same trunk, rings and type roles but drop the map. Errors and the SSH key page are the exceptions: the error page is a line that runs out, and the SSH key is a ticket.

UI primitives come from daisyUI 5: buttons, the navbar and menus, badge, collapse, swap, toast, alert, skeleton and progress. They are themed by two custom themes, line (day) and line-night, which are derived from the site's own tokens, so a token change flows straight through to every primitive. The primitives are flat (depth 0, no noise), drawn with 2px borders and tight radii. The line-diagram pieces (trunk, stations, rings, terminus, the SSH ticket, the error line) stay bespoke and are not daisyUI.

CMS content styling is keyed to semantic elements (h2, blockquote, hr, table, figcaption), so editors can rewrite pages freely without classes. The route strip, the list fold and the freshness badge are progressive enhancements: without scripts the content is complete and intact.
keyCharacteristics: One vertical trunk, stations as ringed nodes, content indented to a fixed content column.
Octilinear geometry only in the map: 45 and 90 degree routes.
Brand purple plus two branch hues; tinted neutrals.
UI primitives are daisyUI, themed from the site's tokens; the line-diagram pieces are hand-drawn.
Flat surfaces, no elevation system; depth comes from the lit trunk, rings and the map's bloom at night.
Every motion has a still equivalent; the page is complete without WebGL2 or JavaScript.
Interior pages ride the same line; CMS content is styled by its semantic elements, so editors can rewrite freely.

rules.name: The Hue Rule
rules.body: Every gray carries hue 324.6 at chroma 0.004 to 0.016. A neutral with no hue does not belong.

rules.name: The One Line, One Color Rule
rules.body: On the home page teal means Writing and amber means Contact. Branch hues are never used decoratively, and no fourth line color is added without a fourth door. On interior pages the same three hues cycle by station position (the Cycle Rule below), the one sanctioned departure.

rules.name: The Cycle Rule
rules.body: Down any interior page, successive stations take Work, Writing, Contact in turn (every third) and then repeat. The end station is Contact.

rules.name: The Underline Rule
rules.body: Links are brand-colored and always underlined; color is never the only cue. Links inside daisyUI buttons and menus are not repainted; the link rule skips them.

rules.name: The Derived Theme Rule
rules.body: daisyUI colours come from the tokens by reference (var(--color-brand-*), var(--color-gray-*), the line hues), never from a copied value, and the stock themes are off.

rules.name: The Signage Rule
rules.body: Only Archivo carries wide, heavy, tight-tracked setting; and only the name uses the 118% width. Text never goes heavy-expanded.

rules.name: The Role Rule
rules.body: New text takes one of the named roles. Heading balance and prose pretty wrapping are on globally.

rules.name: The Flat Line Rule
rules.body: On the line-diagram surfaces, stations and rings are drawn with borders and fills, never shadows.

dos: Do let brand-600 (brand-300 at night) own the trunk, links, name and focus.
Do give any new branch a line color via --line and keep the ring, stub and underline in that color.
Do give every effect a still equivalent: whole lit trunk, finished map frame, whole signature.
Do keep light and dark equal: override colors in the .dark class, not by media query.
Do keep map fades behind type (data-calm regions go to about a tenth strength).
Do open every interior page on a terminus ring and close it on an end station.
Do style CMS content through semantic elements (h2, blockquote, table, hr), never per-page classes, and keep scripted enhancements optional so the content reads whole without scripts.
Do keep the signal tower's shortcuts as real links with the 3D layer purely decorative, and measure station positions from the links in the DOM so labels and drawing never drift.
Do reach for a daisyUI primitive before hand-rolling one, and theme it from the tokens.
Do keep the daisyUI include list tight: add a component to it only when the site uses it.
donts: Don't stack alternating colored bands, hero cards or grids of equal cards on the home page.
Don't introduce neutrals without the brand hue.
Don't wrap interior project or link items in cards; they are rows or image-plus-title on the line.
Don't use heavy expanded Archivo for running text.
Don't add dependencies for an effect; the map is one shader. The exceptions already made: daisyUI for UI primitives, and three.js for the signal tower only.
Don't load three.js on narrow screens or eagerly (it stays a dynamic import behind a min-width 80rem check), and don't put anything interactive on the canvas.
Don't put the direction contract or surface brief into any browser-delivered file.
Don't ship a stock daisyUI theme or data-theme; only line and line-night.
Don't build the trunk, rings, terminus, ticket or error line from daisyUI, and don't hand-roll pills, toggles, chevrons, badges or alerts that a primitive already covers.
